changes.verified: Reproduced at e641797: '[required](missing.md "title")' returned MATCH '1 local' in the disposition's own probe and MATCH '0 local, 0 external' in this reproduction; '' and '[missing]: nothere.md' both returned MATCH '0 local, 0 external'. The control '[required](missing.md)' returned MISMATCH, so the grader discriminated only inside its own narrow pattern.
changes.change: INLINE_LINK_OPENER, REFERENCE_DEFINITION and HTML_RESOURCE_ATTR name three representations the parser does not interpret. An inline-link opener that the supported INLINE_LINK pattern does not also match, a link reference definition, and an HTML src= or href= attribute are each appended to the unsupported list with their line number, so the assertion is INDETERMINATE as runner-interface.md already promised. Nothing attempts to resolve them and no Markdown renderer was added. The grader still reports only the first unsupported representation; that limit is now stated.

changes.verified: Reproduced at e641797: over a four-backtick block quoting a three-backtick example, fenced_lines() marked 5,6,7,9,10 and left line 8 outside, and required_report_fields returned MATCH '1 fields' for a field the document states only inside the example.
changes.change: fence_token() and scan_lines() are one fence reader shared by fenced_lines() and the link grader, so the two cannot drift. A block closes only on a run of the same character at least as long as the opening run, per CommonMark, so a four-backtick block may quote a three-backtick example without ending early. Fence lines themselves remain inside, preserving both callers' prior skip behaviour. The closing-fence info-string rule is not implemented and is not claimed.

changes.verified: Reproduced at e641797: 'description: means the user experience: a schema' returned status 'parsed' with the text stored as the value, and frontmatter_fields returned MATCH 'every required field is a populated scalar'.
changes.change: For an unquoted value the trailing ' #' comment is removed first, exactly as YAML does, and the remainder is then tested for ': ' or a trailing ':'. Either returns status 'unsupported' naming the construct, so frontmatter_fields yields INDETERMINATE 'unparsed' as documented. The grader does not call it a defect: the disclosed limit records that Claude Code 2.1.268 was observed loading such a description on 2026-09-10, so declining to parse is a limit of this reader. Confirmed against PyYAML 6.0.3 in a scratch harness, outside the package: 'k: a: b' and 'k: foo:' both raise ScannerError 'mapping values are not allowed here', while 'k: foo # note: bar' parses to 'foo' and 'k: foo:bar' parses unchanged.
